phase: phase 1 of 2 (measure and propose). The build phase is a separate row and is graded by the P-230 predicate.
missionPremise: P-295 phase 1: measure what a ledger-served surface would have to read before anyone builds the cut-over. A-190 ruled that the atoms question is measured first, after P-230 found that nothing re-runs the bake so a correct ledger write never reaches a customer. The 2026-09-11 ruling (_decisions/2026-09-11_ledger_as_serving_path_seven_steps.md) says a cell is accounting (state, atom reference, provenance, cached rendering keyed to atom and vocabulary version), never a copied value, and that ONE reader in retrieval-api dereferences atoms for every surface.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this close by: (1) reading the four measurements below, each naming its store, its snapshot time, its SQL and its counting rule; (2) re-running the instrument's three commands against the same stores and getting the same shape (cells / atoms / explains / record-timing are all in services/retrieval-api/scripts/ledger-serving-measure.mjs at 4e69f56); (3) checking the PR (https://github.com/empressaioemail-tech/hauska-engine/pull/464) adds the instrument and its self-tests ONLY - three files, +711 lines, all under services/retrieval-api/; (4) reading the proposal and the named conflicts with the 2026-09-11 ruling and being able to disagree with any of them on the numbers.
scopeBasis: hauska-engine only, exactly as the dispatch scopes it: a fresh clone at P:/tmp/p295-ledger-serving on branch measure/p295-ledger-serving from origin/main e7cd0aee (the dispatch was compiled against d88cf65 and MOST-CURRENT SOURCE WINS put the clone two days further on). The lane read the factory store, the atoms store, the deployed retrieval-api and two product checkouts read-only. It wrote no store, minted no atom, edited no reader or writer, deployed nothing, and launched no sub-agents (FAN-DEPTH 0).

m1_cellShapePerRail.sql: SET statement_timeout='1500000'; SET default_transaction_read_only=on; COPY (SELECT rail_key, coalesce(cell_state->>'kind','(no-kind)') AS kind, coalesce(cell_state->>'source','(no-source)') AS source, (cell_state ?| array['atomDid','atom_did','atomRef','atom_ref','atomDids','atomRefs','atomVersion','atom_version']) AS has_pointer, count(*) AS cells FROM parcel_record_cell WHERE place_key >= '<fips>:' AND place_key < '<fips+1>:' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) TO STDOUT WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true);  -- one statement per county on the (place_key, rail_key) primary key
m1_cellShapePerRail.answer: 65 rails x 981,405 parcels = 63,791,325 cells, and the kind buckets sum to exactly that (completeness check). value 26,814,129 / unaccounted 22,397,221 / not-applicable 7,425,002 / absent-verified 6,765,819 / refused 389,154. Of the 26,814,129 value cells, 0 carry an atom reference of ANY candidate spelling. 46 rails carry value cells, 19 carry none. The setback rails carry 18 distinct writers each; maxHeightFt 13; the envelope rails 6.
m1_cellShapePerRail.headline: 0 of 26,814,129. Every rail is value-copied-only, so retrieval-api's extractAtomDid (parcel-record-reader.ts:63-67) has never fired against live data.

m2_atomsForTheLedgerWrittenRails.theCrossTabThatDecidesIt: Of the 378 sampled parcels, 193 have a setbackFrontFt cell with kind 'value'. Of those 193, 119 (61.7%) have a setback-rule atom and 74 (38.3%) have none at all. Of the 119 with both, the atom's front value AGREES with the cell's copied value on 83 (69.8%) and DISAGREES on 36 (30.2%) - and all 36 run the same way: the cell carries the LARGER front setback (Bastrop contributes 11, every one 'cell 30 ft vs atom 25 ft'). No vintage comparison is made, so this is a disagreement count and not a finding about which side is newer (every sampled atom was written 2026-07-24 or earlier while the cells' vintage stamps reach 2026-09-15, which is a HINT and is labelled one).
m2_atomsForTheLedgerWrittenRails.headline: Atoms exist for SOME rails and not others, and where they exist they do not agree with what the cells have already copied in. A dereferencing cut-over would serve nothing on 38.3% of the parcels whose cell carries a number, and would CHANGE the number on 30.2% of those where both exist.

falsifier: 1. Both directions: PASS - 19 self-tests in src/__tests__/ledger-serving-measure.test.ts, run against the SAME classification function the live measurement used; the negative direction is the live shape (26,814,129 value cells classified copied-only), not a fixture shape; plus non-vacuity (a null/blank pointer is not a reference; a nested pointer is not counted) and the assertion that the emitted SQL's pointer array equals the TypeScript vocabulary so the two cannot drift. Measured locally: services/retrieval-api 20 files / 157 tests pass, tsc --noEmit clean. 2. The atoms query plan uses an index: PASS - 'Index Scan using atoms_entity_composite_unique on atoms  (cost=0.69..8.71 rows=1 width=65)' pasted verbatim above; the unindexed-by-intuition spelling is pasted beside it at cost 10143.38..11021.14. 3. The /record timing covers at least three counties: PASS at four.
contradicted: The dispatch's own context block, in two places, and both in the direction of 'this is cheaper and more knowable than it looked'. (a) 'P-230's attempt to check whether matching atoms exist timed out after about 120 s on a per-parcel entity_id lookup' - measured: 378 parcels x 4 entity types = 1,512 point lookups complete in 0.7-1.4 s per county on atoms_entity_composite_unique. The 120 s was not the index; something else in that attempt was. (b) The premise that the ambiguity is 'do atoms exist' - they do, for 100% of sampled parcels as zoning-fact, and the real, decision-shaped finding is that they DISAGREE with the copied values on 30.2% of the parcels where both exist (a consistent one-directional signature) and are missing on 38.3% of the parcels whose cell carries a setback number. Also contradicted from the ruling's side: 'one reader in retrieval-api' is three readers on disk, and the extra two are not new - one of them is what serves the customer today.

proposal.railsThatCanServeFromTheCellsThroughTheR: NONE in the sense the 2026-09-11 ruling means (dereference an atom): 26,814,129 value cells, 0 pointers, nothing to dereference. What could serve today is the copied value plus its provenance fields, which is what the ruling says a cell is not.
railsThatNeedAtomsMintedFirst: maxHeightFt / maxFootprintSqFt / maxLotCoveragePct / maxImperviousCoverPct: pointer AND atom coverage both missing (gate not slated for any of them; only 271/378 sampled parcels have a buildable-envelope atom; 120/378 carry a maxHeightFt value cell).

the setback group: the atom exists for only 61.7% of the parcels whose cell carries a value (74/193 missing) and disagrees on 30.2% of those where it does (36/119), so this rail needs BOTH minting and an adjudication rule.

zoningDistrict / zoningJurisdictionKey / zoningProvenance: the only rails whose canonical claim already exists for every sampled parcel (zoning-fact 378/378). These three are the rails that can be repointed first, ahead of any minting work.
proposal.howACachedRenderingWouldKeyToTheCellVers: It cannot today, and that is a schema fact rather than an opinion: parcel_record_cell is (place_key text, rail_key text, cell_state jsonb, updated_at timestamptz) and nothing else - no pointer column, no version column. The only version-ish field is updated_at, a wall-clock stamp, and the cell_state's own 'vintage' field is the SOURCE's date (2026-09-15T00:54:11.683Z on 48209:100226's setback cell), not a content version of the cell. A rendering keyed to 'atom version and vocabulary version' needs the pointer and a content version to exist first; both belong in P-163's scope, not this lane's.
retirementOrderForTheBake: 1. Land the writer (P-163: pointer plus content version in cell_state). Nothing can key to anything until it exists.

2. Repoint LDT's parcelRecordCellRead.ts onto retrieval-api's reader, so the two stop being parallel implementations of the same read; this is the consumer that already serves a customer from the ledger.

3. Repoint the map's atom-chain adapter (hauska-map atom-chain-to-facets.ts:487-518) - it is the surface the customer sees and the one reading atoms instead of cells, which is why the panel and the MCP disagree today.

4. Retire the bake per RAIL, not per county, with a divergence test in the overlap; for the setback group the divergence already exists (cell 30 vs atom 25) and the test cannot be written until someone picks a side.
5. Only then retire the legacy derive (legacy-design-tools buildableEnvelope/derive.ts:220).
conflictsWithThe2026_09_11Ruling: The ruling says a cell is accounting, 'never a copied value'. On disk 26,814,129 value cells ARE copied values with no pointer. Either the ruling needs a named transition window in which the copied value is permitted while the pointer is absent, or every consumer repoint is blocked behind the writer. RECOMMEND THE OPERATOR RULE: the copied value is permitted ONLY while the pointer is absent, and its presence is itself a measured defect this instrument reports (so the count cannot be forgotten), until the writer lands.

The ruling says 'one reader in retrieval-api'. There are three, and one of them is what serves customers today. A lane that builds the retrieval-api reader without a ruled retirement order adds a fourth diverging producer. RECOMMEND THE OPERATOR RULE the five-step retirement order above, in that order.

The ruling's 'cached rendering keyed to atom version and vocabulary version' has no version to key to in parcel_record_cell; the only candidate is updated_at, which is a wall clock. RECOMMEND the operator fold a content version into P-163's scope explicitly, because a rendering cache built today would key to updated_at and fail silently in exactly the way this program keeps finding.

pr.ciNote: One check exists on this repo's PR workflow at this head; it is the only entry in statusCheckRollup, and it is SUCCESS. Locally the same package runs 20 files / 157 tests green; the monorepo-wide `pnpm -r test` has pre-existing failures in packages/engine-core on this machine (a site-plan test timing out at 20 s and PASS/FAIL expectation cases) that this PR cannot reach, since it adds files under services/retrieval-api/ only.

leave_behind: The instrument is now the cheap way to answer the two questions P-230 and P-293R could not: `pnpm exec tsx services/retrieval-api/scripts/ledger-serving-measure.mjs cells --county <fips>` reports the pointer count per rail for a county in 5-270 s, and `atoms --sample <csv>` resolves 4 entity types per parcel by index in ~1 s per county.

The pointer-spelling question is closed for the FULL population: 8 candidate spellings tested across all 63,791,325 cells, 0 hits. If a writer later introduces one, m1's byKind/has_pointer buckets move and the instrument says so on the next county run.

The unindexed spelling of the atoms question (body->>'parcelNodeId') looks right and plans badly (BitmapAnd at ~10,143..11,021, estimating 31,591 rows for one parcelNodeId). Whoever writes the pointer read should use (entity_type, entity_id), which is exactly the pair the atom's own entity_id already is.

MAX-HEIGHT and the envelope rails have a THIRD state this lane did not know existed before reading the code: the serve-cutover wrapper is merged and inert (maxHeightFtFactServeCutover.ts:9-11 - not slated, fails the gate on every in-scope county, blocked on the 3,376-parcel zoningDistrict residual). If that residual clears, the wrapper starts serving the ledger with no further code change. That is a live trigger sitting on a shelf and it deserves a named owner.

The 36/36 one-directional front-setback disagreement (cell larger than atom, Bastrop 'cell 30 vs atom 25') is a concrete, reproducible probe for whoever adjudicates which side is canonical: 48021:103387, and 48021:104119-104131 for the cluster.

A rendering cache cannot key to a cell version today (parcel_record_cell has place_key, rail_key, cell_state, updated_at and nothing else). Naming that in P-163's scope now is cheaper than discovering it while building the cache.

The county place_key prefix range does not cost the same per row in every county (Travis 268 s vs McLennan 5 s for the same statement shape at different sample depths); a per-county scan budget cannot be a constant.
disclosures: MISTAKE, DISCLOSED: one probe against the 199 GB atoms table was launched without an index (SELECT ... ORDER BY fetched_at DESC LIMIT 1) during reconnaissance and was killed within ~35 s. It wrote nothing and read no user data; it was replaced by an indexed point lookup. No other statement in this lane ran without statement_timeout and default_transaction_read_only=on.

CP1 was filed after the instrument's first draft rather than strictly before (see CP1.phaseNote). No store write, no atom mint, no reader or writer edit and no deploy happened at any point in this lane, so nothing downstream was set by the ordering.

The M2 answer is a 378-parcel SAMPLE with a large county-level spread (setback-rule atoms 0/50 in McLennan, 40/60 in Bastrop) and is reported with its own denominators; it must not be read as a statewide rate.

The LDT citations are at origin/main 62e7349b, read with git show, because the local LDT checkout sits on a branch that does not contain the serve-cutover loaders. Citing the local tree would have answered 'no surface reads the ledger' and been wrong.

The /record timing is the DEPLOYED revision, which serves the factory store and dereferences nothing (no pointer exists to dereference). It answers 'what a cold read costs now', not 'what it will cost once cells carry pointers'.

The /record calls from this machine needed NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca (the local trust store is not in Node's bundle: UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE). The workaround is in the run command, not hard-coded into the instrument.
